newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Bottom-fishing, Dow give mixed view for Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Bottom-fishing, Dow give mixed view for Singapore.

text.p: A return of funds into the Singapore stock market as they bottom-fish blue chips and banks may underpin the market on Tuesday, dealers said.

But the buying could be cooled by the sharp drop overnight on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones industrial average fell 192.25 points to 7,604.26, a point decline second only to the 508-point plunge when the market crashed on October 19, 1987.
Dealers also warned that Monday's late surge in index-linked stocks and banks in Singapore on fund buying might not be the harbinger for the long awaited market rebound. Fund buying remained limited.
"It is a good time to look at some stocks because of their attractive valuation. But I think it would be premature to say the market has turned around. Volume has been thin," said a dealer.
The Straits Times Industrials Index ended 26.35 points up at 2,034.79 on Monday.
